title: Shared-GPU slab allocation and soft-quota enforcement for tenant isolation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Tenants on Dedicated pools sometimes experience noisy neighbor effects when multiple small workloads share GPUs. Current hard partitioning reduces utilization and drives cost up. We need a mechanism that improves utilization while enforcing tenant separation and predictable throughput guarantees.

Proposal: Implement a slab-based GPU allocation layer combined with soft-quotas and a two-stage enforcement policy. Slabs are fractional GPU allocations (e.g., 1/8, 1/4, 1/2, full) that can be assigned to tenant queues. Tenants receive a soft quota in slabs plus a burst allowance. If usage exceeds soft quota for a sustained window, the scheduler triggers one of: autoscale (request extra dedicated slabs), token-bucket slowdown (soft-throttle), or graceful preemption of best-effort jobs. This preserves tail latency for SLO-backed tenants while increasing overall GPU utilization.

Goals: (1) tenant isolation with bounded interference, (2) higher utilization vs strict hard tenancy, (3) predictable throughput guarantees and SLA-aligned throttles, (4) integration with autoscaler and billing/quotas for accounting.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler can allocate slabs (1/8, 1/4, 1/2, 1) across nodes and report allocation metadata per tenant.
Soft-quota enforcement: no tenant exceeds configured soft quota for more than 5 minutes without autoscaler action or explicit escalation.
Burst handling: tenants can burst above soft quota for short windows (configurable), and bursts are correctly billed and logged.
Noisy-neighbor mitigation: tail latency for SLO-backed tenants increases by <= 5% in mixed workloads vs baseline hard-partition baseline.
Autoscaler integration: when soft quota exceeded, autoscaler suggestions are emitted and can trigger reservation flows in Dedicated control plane.
E2E tests: integration tests in CI simulate multi-tenant mixed loads and validate eviction, throttle, and autoscale flows.
Monitoring: dashboards surfaced per-tenant for slab usage, queued requests, throttle events, preemptions, and billing counters.
Canary rollout in eu-west-1 with 5 pilot customers before global rollout.
technical_notes: Slab model: map tensors/streams to fractional GPU slices using cgroup-like accounting at the serving runtime surface; prefer existing MIG support where hardware provides it.
Fair-share policy: primary constraint is 'guaranteed slabs' per tenant, secondary is priority score for best-effort jobs; tie-breaker is fairness window (default 15m).
Soft vs hard quotas: soft quotas allow bursts with token-bucket tracking; hard quotas are enforced only for emergency isolation mode.

Preemption: implement graceful preemption for best-effort queues by signaling existing workers to checkpoint and draining KV cache where possible; avoid immediate process kill unless in emergency mode.
Autoscaler API: extend existing Dedicated autoscaler to accept 'slab' capacity requests and return ETA for allocation. Autoscaler should prefer colocated free slabs before spinning up new instances.
Accounting: emit slab-seconds per tenant for billing downstream; include burst and preempted work counters.
Kernel/runtime changes: add lightweight scheduler hook in runtime to refuse new streams when target slab budget exhausted and to tag responses with 'throttle_reason' for observability.
Trade-offs: slab model increases scheduling complexity and slightly more metadata per request; but reduces need for large capacity commits and improves utilization for small tenants.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Dev): prototype slab accounting in local cluster and unit tests (complete).
Phase 1 (Canary): enable in eu-west-1 on a single Dedicated pool with 5 pilot tenants; autoscaler suggestions are advisory only (safe mode).
Phase 2 (Beta): turn on soft-quota enforcement with reduced aggressiveness; collect telemetry and customer feedback; enable billing counters but not bill for bursts yet.
Phase 3 (GA): enable full soft-quota enforcement and charging for bursts; expand to remaining regions with scheduler fallback policies enabled.
Rollback: global feature flag at control plane; can revert to hard partitions per-pool.
testing_plan: Unit tests for slab accounting and token-bucket logic.
Integration tests that simulate 20 tenants with mixed SLOs and validate no tenant exceeds soft quota beyond threshold.
Chaos test: random node kills and MIG eviction to ensure graceful preemption and autoscaler reconciliation.
Load test: stress mixed workloads to compare utilization against current hard-partition baseline and measure tail latency changes.
Billing test: verify slab-seconds and burst counters in billing pipeline match simulated usage.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike complete; prototype runtime hook implemented to attach slab metadata to streams. - Marco

2026-03-06: Implemented token-bucket burst allowance and basic throttle response code path. Added metrics for 'slab_used' and 'burst_tokens'. - Marco
2026-03-08: Integration test skeleton added; initial CI job failing due to race in preemption path. Investigating. - Marco
2026-03-10: Resolved race by serializing preemption signals at scheduler step; added e2e test for graceful preemption. Preparing canary config. - Marco
2026-03-12: Canary config ready; autoscaler advisory API PR open for review. Security review scheduled next week. - Aisha
estimated_cost_savings: $0.12 per slab-second projected at 25% uplift in utilization vs strict partitions
notes: Keep canary config limited to non-critical customers. Post-canary retrospective to capture any unexpected billing or SLO regressions. Ensure ops runbook for manual emergency hard-partition revert exists.
